ig_caption:
Your database just got a public IP 😬 One line did it: type: LoadBalancer

AI wrote this Kubernetes manifest:
⚠️ the Postgres Service is type: LoadBalancer → on AKS / EKS / GKE that's an internet-facing IP
⚠️ the password is the default ("postgres"), in plain text

In the demo, a stranger outside the cluster logs in and reads the customer table.

The fix:
✅ database Services stay ClusterIP
✅ a NetworkPolicy lets only the app's pods in
✅ a generated password, kept in a Secret

Same login from outside → nothing there.

Is your database Service ClusterIP? Tell me 👇

yt_title: AI exposed this database with one line of Kubernetes YAML #kubernetes
yt_description:
One line, type: LoadBalancer, on a database Service. On a cloud cluster (AKS, EKS, GKE) that creates an internet-facing IP for your database.

Demo (local kind cluster; LoadBalancer IPs from cloud-provider-kind; customer rows are fake):
- from outside the cluster: psql login with the default password, then select * from customers
- fix: Service type ClusterIP, a NetworkPolicy allowing only the app's pods, and a generated password stored in a Secret
- same login from outside after the fix: no route to host

From "Would You Ship This?": AI-written infrastructure gets a real code review. Follow for more.
